record.context_brief: Existential copies of F_2 inside groups
record.original_question: Does there exist a discrete group G containing an existential copy of the free group F_2 such that the group von Neumann algebra L(G) is not isomorphic to L(F_n) for some n ∈ N? More specifically, does there exist a non-elementary surface group G with L(G) not isomorphic to any L(F_n)?

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Does there exist a group G that contains an existential inclusion of F2 such that L(G) ≇ L(Fn) for some n ∈ N? Specifically, does there exist a non elementary surface group G such that L(G) ≇ L(Fn)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(1) For a discrete group $G$, the (left) group von Neumann algebra $L(G)$ is the von Neumann algebra generated by the left regular representation of $G$ on $\ell^2(G)$. When $G$ is i.c.c. (every nontrivial conjugacy class is infinite), $L(G)$ is a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with canonical trace $\tau(x) = \langle x \delta_e, \delta_e\rangle$.

(2) Let $F_n$ denote the free group on $n$ generators ($2 \le n \le \infty$). The factors $L(F_n)$ are the free group factors.

(3) An inclusion of groups $H \le G$ is called an existential inclusion (and $H$ is called an existential copy of itself in $G$) if for every existential first-order formula $\varphi(x_1,\dots,x_k)$ in the language of groups and every tuple $h_1,\dots,h_k \in H$, one has
$$H \models \varphi(h_1,\dots,h_k) \iff G \models \varphi(h_1,\dots,h_k).$$
Equivalently, $H$ is existentially closed in $G$: every finite system of equations and inequations with parameters in $H$ that has a solution in $G$ already has a solution in $H$.

(4) A surface group is the fundamental group $\pi_1(\Sigma_g)$ of a closed orientable surface of genus $g \ge 1$; it is called non-elementary if $g \ge 2$ (so that the group is non-abelian and hyperbolic).

Questions.

(a) Does there exist a discrete group $G$ which contains an existential copy of $F_2$ and such that $L(G) \not\cong L(F_n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$?

(b) More specifically, does there exist a non-elementary surface group $G$ such that $L(G) \not\cong L(F_n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$?
artifact.category_tag: II_1 factors and free group factors
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is closely tied to the long-standing free group factor isomorphism problem, which remains open. Whether the group von Neumann algebra of a non-elementary surface group is isomorphic to some $L(F_n)$ is a known open question; no result in the literature settles it, and it is listed among current open problems on ultraproduct II_1 factors. Status: open.

status_evidence.title: Free group factor isomorphism problem (Wikipedia: Von Neumann algebra)
status_evidence.snippet: Whether L(F_n) and L(F_m) are isomorphic for n ≠ m ≥ 2 is a famous open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The free group factor isomorphism problem, with which this question is intertwined, is still open.
